The snapshot directory named task is not treated as the product slug. task.toml:6 describes a JavaScript/HTML playground with isolated execution, preview recovery and a shared revision-history library; instruction.md:1-3 and environment/instructions/behaviour.md:5-15,25-40 explicitly request those axes. The hard difficulty explanation at task.toml:10-11 accurately identifies isolation, unfinished-run cancellation, preview recovery and multi-editor consistency. Programming category, product keywords, provenance naming Colderwater, and arena_slice at :7,12-15 remain coherent with tests/app_context.md:3 and the reference. Stack labels describe the supplied reference: package.json:14-19 has Express/SQLite/TypeScript/Vite, src/app.tsx:1-6,108 imports React and constructs the editor. Frontend tools remain optional in integration.md:3. No criterion count or measured performance claim appears in the metadata. Absence of task.version is permitted by the workbook and staged contract:77. All 21 indexed artifact hashes match; their scripted product scope does not establish judge or portal results. Row 8 is decidable from these source bytes and requires no runtime measurement.
counterexample: Broken-app challenge (source reasoning): a static page with the correct Colderwater branding can satisfy identity alone, which is appropriate because row 8 does not certify working behavior; copied calculator/store metadata would fail the explicit brief-versus-metadata comparison. Conforming alternative: a working playground using a different permitted frontend or layout is not excluded by this identity verdict; integration.md:3 and policy.md:5 explicitly leave those choices open, and reference-stack keywords do not create an extra public requirement.
